pr_body:
Fix #40705

#29748 added `DefaultHttpContext._active` and set it in `DefaultHttpContext.Initialize(IFeatureCollection)`. The problem is that this method only gets called via `DefaultHttpContextFactory.Initialize(DefaultHttpContext httpContext, IFeatureCollection featureCollection)` and not `DefaultHttpContextFactory.Create(IFeatureCollection featureCollection)` which uses `DefaultHttpContextFactory.Initialize(DefaultHttpContext httpContext)` instead of the variant of `Initialize` that takes the `IFeatureCollection`.

This change gets rid of `DefaultHttpContextFactory.Initialize(DefaultHttpContext httpContext)`, inlining its content into its caller, and changes `Create` to use that one.

issue_context.title: DefaultHttpContextFactory.Create(IFeatureCollection) does not set DefaultHttpContext._active
issue_context.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

#29748 added `DefaultHttpContext._active` and set it in `DefaultHttpContext.Initialize(IFeattureCollection)`. The problem is that this method only gets called via `DefaultHttpContextFactory.Initialize(DefaultHttpContext httpContext, IFeatureCollection featureCollection)` and not `DefaultHttpContextFactory.Create(IFeatureCollection featureCollection)`.

This means that the first unpooled request over a given Kestrel connection is never marked `_active.` And since `IISHttpContextOfT<TContext>` does not implement `IHostContextContainer<TContext>`, `_active` is never set for requests coming in over IIS.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/54385/158269341-a32aed75-e25b-409d-80f6-6dec26f365e8.png)

This means those using memory dump analyzers have to go back to looking if `_features` is zeroed out instead of looking at `_active` which was intended to be the easier way to do this but is currently misleading.

### Expected Behavior

`DefaultHttpContext._active` should be set for all ongoing requests served by both IIS and Kestrel if the `DefaultHttpContextFactory` is in use.

### Steps To Reproduce

Attach a debugger to an ASP.NET Core app using IIS or Kestrel. Inspect the `HttpContext` of a request which should be a `DefaultHttpCotnext`. With Kestrel, `DefaultHttpContext._active` won't be set for the first request sent over a connection (or any other unpooled request). With IIS, `DefaultHttpContext._active` is never set.

### Exceptions (if any)

_No response_

### .NET Version

7.0.100-preview.3.22163.1

### Anything else?

_No response_
